statement: Re-dispatching onto an existing branch is blocked when that branch carries committed work not reachable from any remote, unless `--adopt-branch` is passed; the reachability test checks every remote, not just origin, so re-dispatch to a repository the operator cannot push to is not incorrectly blocked.

source.quote:
if git -C "$repo_path" show-ref --verify --quiet "refs/heads/$BRANCH" 2>/dev/null; then
        # Guard: if the existing branch carries committed work that is not
        # reachable from any remote, a prior interrupted dispatch may have done
        # real work.  Block re-dispatch until the coordinator reconciles, to
        # prevent duplicate or lost effort.
        #
        # Reachability from ANY remote is the test.  Comparing against only
        # "refs/remotes/origin/$BRANCH" used to make this fire for every branch
        # that had never been pushed, which blocked resuming preserved work in
        # any repository the operator cannot push to (td-7f3a9a).
        prior_commits="$(_sgt_branch_unpushed_commits "$repo_path" "$BRANCH")"
        if [[ -n "$prior_commits" && "$ADOPT_BRANCH" -ne 1 ]]; then
          _die "Branch $BRANCH already has committed work not reachable from any remote. Re-run with --adopt-branch to resume it, which checks the branch out at a new worktree and preserves every commit. Commits found:
$prior_commits"
        fi
        if [[ -n "$prior_commits" ]]; then
          _info "adopting existing branch $BRANCH with preserved commits:"
          printf '%s\n' "$prior_commits" | sed 's/^/      /'
        fi

trigger: the target branch already exists and may carry prior uncommitted-upstream work
outcome: prior committed work is never silently overwritten or orphaned by a fresh dispatch; resuming it requires an explicit --adopt-branch
notes: Consequence-class: safety/recovery — prevents duplicate or lost effort by blocking re-dispatch onto a branch with unreachable-from-any-remote committed work, requiring explicit adoption; checking every remote (not just origin) fixed a prior bug (td-7f3a9a) that mis-blocked unpushable repos.

statement: After acquiring a worktree, dispatch requires the worktree's `.git` to be a real (non-symlinked) file containing a well-formed `gitdir:` pointer, and resolves and records both the pointer and the canonicalized git directory, failing closed if either check does not hold.

source.quote:
[[ -f "$worktree_path/.git" && ! -L "$worktree_path/.git" ]] || \
    _die "worktree has no immutable Git pointer: $worktree_path"
  worktree_git_pointer="$(cat "$worktree_path/.git")"
  [[ "$worktree_git_pointer" == "gitdir: "* ]] || \
    _die "worktree Git pointer is malformed: $worktree_path/.git"
  worktree_git_dir="${worktree_git_pointer#gitdir: }"
  if [[ "$worktree_git_dir" != /* ]]; then
    worktree_git_dir="$worktree_path/$worktree_git_dir"
  fi
  worktree_git_dir="$(cd "$worktree_git_dir" 2>/dev/null && pwd -P)" || \
    _die "worktree Git directory is unavailable: $worktree_git_dir"
  printf '%s\n' "$worktree_git_pointer" > "$repo_task_dir/worktree_git_pointer"
  printf '%s\n' "$worktree_git_dir" > "$repo_task_dir/worktree_git_dir"

statement: If any step of spawning a worker fails — no pane returned, a notification-target creation race, failure to capture exact pane identity, or the worker not acknowledging its durable notification in time — dispatch stops any Claude background session the worker may have started, kills the pane, marks the repo `orphaned` with a named diagnostic, and hands off to `sgt-td-memory` before dying, rather than leaving an ambiguous or silently-failed worker.

source.quote:
initial_notification_id="$(dd if=/dev/urandom bs=16 count=1 2>/dev/null | od -An -tx1 | tr -d ' \n')"
  _sgt_publish_worker_notification "$repo_task_dir" "$worktree_path" \
    "$initial_notification_id" initial "Read the .sergeant-brief.md file and execute the mission."
  WORKER_RUN_CMD="$(_sgt_worker_command \
    "$SCRIPT_DIR/sgt-interactive-worker" "$repo_task_dir" "$worktree_path" "$AGENT_CMD")"
  if pane_target="$(tmux new-window -P -F '#{pane_id}' -t "$TMUX_SESSION:" \
    -n "$WINDOW_NAME" -c "$worktree_path" "$WORKER_RUN_CMD")"; then
    if [[ -z "$pane_target" ]]; then
      printf 'orphaned\n' > "$repo_task_dir/status"
      printf 'tmux launched no worker pane\n' > "$repo_task_dir/diagnostic"
      "$SCRIPT_DIR/sgt-td-memory" handoff "$repo_task_dir" "$worktree_path" || true
      _die "tmux returned no pane for $rname"
    fi
    printf '%s\n' "$pane_target" > "$repo_task_dir/pane"
    if pane_identity="$(_sgt_pane_identity "$pane_target")" && [[ -n "$pane_identity" ]]; then
      _sgt_replace_owned_file "$repo_task_dir/pane_identity" "$pane_identity" || \
        _die "Could not publish worker pane identity"
      if ! _sgt_notification_target_create "$repo_task_dir" "$initial_notification_id" \
          "$pane_identity" >/dev/null; then
        # Claude-specific backstop: stop any background session the worker may
        # already have launched before the notification target race was detected.
        _sgt_claude_stop_bg_session "$repo_task_dir"
        tmux kill-pane -t "$pane_target" 2>/dev/null || true
        printf 'orphaned\n' > "$repo_task_dir/status"
        printf 'notification target creation race: concurrent dispatch detected\n' > "$repo_task_dir/diagnostic"
        "$SCRIPT_DIR/sgt-td-memory" handoff "$repo_task_dir" "$worktree_path" || true
        _die "notification target race detected for $rname; worker orphaned"
      fi
    else
      # Claude-specific backstop: stop any background session the worker may
      # already have launched before the pane identity capture failed.
      _sgt_claude_stop_bg_session "$repo_task_dir"
      tmux kill-pane -t "$pane_target" 2>/dev/null || true
      printf 'orphaned\n' > "$repo_task_dir/status"
      printf 'tmux failed to capture exact worker pane identity\n' > "$repo_task_dir/diagnostic"
      "$SCRIPT_DIR/sgt-td-memory" handoff "$repo_task_dir" "$worktree_path" || true
      _die "tmux failed to capture exact worker pane identity for $rname"
    fi
    if ! _sgt_wait_worker_notification "$pane_target" "$repo_task_dir" "$initial_notification_id"; then
      # Claude-specific backstop: stop any background session the worker may
      # have launched before the notification acknowledgement timed out.
      _sgt_claude_stop_bg_session "$repo_task_dir"
      tmux kill-pane -t "$pane_target" 2>/dev/null || true
      printf 'orphaned\n' > "$repo_task_dir/status"
      printf 'interactive worker did not acknowledge its durable notification\n' > "$repo_task_dir/diagnostic"
      "$SCRIPT_DIR/sgt-td-memory" handoff "$repo_task_dir" "$worktree_path" || true
      _die "interactive worker notification acknowledgement timed out for $rname"
    fi
  else
    printf 'orphaned\n' > "$repo_task_dir/status"
    printf 'tmux failed to launch worker supervisor\n' > "$repo_task_dir/diagnostic"
    "$SCRIPT_DIR/sgt-td-memory" handoff "$repo_task_dir" "$worktree_path" || true
    _die "tmux failed to launch worker supervisor for $rname"
  fi

statement: Every target repo is validated (cloned, td initialized) before any task is created, specifically so that a prerequisite failure never requires rolling back an already-created task.

source.quote:
# Validate every target before creating any task so prerequisite failures do
# not require rollback.
for rname in "${TARGET_REPOS[@]}"; do
  for ((i=0; i<repo_count; i++)); do
    n="$(yq ".repos[$i].name" "$CONFIG_FILE")"
    [[ "$n" == "$rname" ]] && break
  done

  raw_path="$(yq ".repos[$i].path" "$CONFIG_FILE")"
  repo_path="$(_resolve_path "$raw_path")"

  _sgt_is_git_repo "$repo_path" || _rollback_or_die "repo '$rname' is not cloned at $repo_path"
  if ! td_check="$(td list --json --work-dir "$repo_path" --limit 1 2>&1)"; then
    if [[ "$td_check" == *"database not found: run 'td init' first"* ]]; then
      _rollback_or_die "td is not initialized in repo '$rname' ($repo_path). Run: td init --work-dir '$repo_path'"
    fi
    _rollback_or_die "td prerequisite check failed in repo '$rname' ($repo_path): $td_check"
  fi
done

statement: A worker follows a notification instruction exactly once per token; repeated nudges carrying the same token are treated as retries, not new work.

statement: One shared harness registry defines the accepted-harness capability gate, the readiness probe, and the launch invocation together, so the three can never drift out of sync with each other.

# bin/sgt-interactive-worker: the accepted-harness capability gate, the
# readiness probe, and the launch invocation.  They drifted, and `claude` ended
# up accepted by the gate and launchable while being permanently unable to
# satisfy readiness — so its notification was never injected.  One registry now
# drives all three, and _sgt_harness_registry_validate fails loudly when a row
# omits a probe or names a probe that is not implemented.

notes: Mechanism: previously these three facts were described in three separate places inside bin/sgt-interactive-worker and drifted, letting claude be accepted and launchable while unable to ever satisfy readiness.

statement: Harness registry validation rejects a row that is malformed or does not declare both a harness name and a readiness probe, naming the offending row and the expected format in the error.

statement: The opencode and oc harnesses are launched with --dangerously-skip-permissions by deliberate security-posture decision: the operator's consent is scoped to the intent file and worker brief reviewed and approved at dispatch time, not to per-action interactive confirmation, and the worker cannot escalate beyond that dispatch-time-approved scope.

# The opencode harness is launched with --dangerously-skip-permissions.

  # in an automated dispatch context, not an interactive session. The operator
  # approves scope at dispatch time through the intent file and worker brief

  # prompts so the worker can proceed autonomously.  Operator trust is scoped
  # to the intent file reviewed and approved at dispatch time; the worker
  # cannot escalate beyond that scope.  See docs/using-sergeant.md for the
  # full security model.
  printf '%s\n' \
    'opencode:tui:--dangerously-skip-permissions' \
    'oc:tui:--dangerously-skip-permissions' \
    'goose:tui:session' \
    'claude:tui:'

statement: The intent revision is computed as a SHA-256 digest of the intent file's contents, using shasum or sha256sum, and fails with an actionable error if neither tool is available.

source.quote:
_sgt_intent_revision() {
  local intent_file="$1"
  if command -v shasum >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    shasum -a 256 "$intent_file" | awk '{print $1}'
  elif command -v sha256sum >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    sha256sum "$intent_file" | awk '{print $1}'
  else
    printf 'ERROR: shasum or sha256sum is required\n' >&2
    return 1
  fi
}

statement: The set of flags no-mistakes' axi run subcommand accepts is discovered by parsing its own --help output, not by inferring capability from a version number.

source.quote:
# Flag names accepted by `no-mistakes axi run`, space-delimited and space-padded.
# Help output is the only capability surface no-mistakes exposes, so the probe
# reads it rather than inferring support from a version number.
_sgt_no_mistakes_axi_run_flags() {
  local flags
  flags="$(no-mistakes axi run --help 2>&1 | \
    sed -n 's/^[[:space:]]\{2,\}\(-[A-Za-z], \)\{0,1\}\(--[a-z][a-z-]*\).*/\2/p' | \
    sort -u | tr '\n' ' ')"
  [[ -n "$flags" ]] || return 1
  printf ' %s\n' "$flags"
}

outcome: canonical intent content defaults to never appearing in argv/ps/proc, and only reaches argv when the operator explicitly opted in for that run
notes: Consequence-class: safety/human-decision — a privacy-sensitive default with an explicit, non-durable (flag, not env var) consent gate for the riskier path.

statement: A coordinator-owned validation run only proceeds if the fleet-level, repo-state-level, and worktree-level copies of .sergeant-intent.md are byte-identical to each other AND their recorded revision hashes agree AND that revision re-verifies against the fleet copy's actual current content.

source.quote:
_sgt_intent_revision_matches() {
  local task_dir="$1" repo_state="$2" worktree="$3"
  local fleet_intent="$task_dir/.sergeant-intent.md"
  local repo_intent="$repo_state/.sergeant-intent.md"
  local worktree_intent="$worktree/.sergeant-intent.md"
  local fleet_revision="$task_dir/intent_revision"
  local repo_revision="$repo_state/intent_revision"
  local expected_revision

  [[ -f "$fleet_intent" && -f "$repo_intent" && -f "$worktree_intent" ]] || return 1
  [[ -f "$fleet_revision" && -f "$repo_revision" ]] || return 1
  cmp -s "$fleet_intent" "$repo_intent" && cmp -s "$fleet_intent" "$worktree_intent" || return 1
  expected_revision="$(cat "$fleet_revision")"
  [[ -n "$expected_revision" && "$expected_revision" == "$(cat "$repo_revision")" ]] || return 1
  [[ "$expected_revision" == "$(_sgt_intent_revision "$fleet_intent")" ]]
}

trigger: sgt-validate checks whether the canonical intent revision matches before launching
outcome: any divergence between the three intent copies, or between a recorded revision and the file's real hash, blocks validation rather than validating a possibly-stale or inconsistent intent
notes: Consequence-class: identity — an identity (intent content) pinned at dispatch time must be honored exactly at a later re-entry (validation), not silently substituted.

statement: An intent file path is rejected as unsafe if any path component along its resolved chain — not just the final component — is itself a symlink.

source.quote:
_sgt_intent_path_has_symlink() {
  local input_file="$1" current component
  local -a components
  if [[ "$input_file" == /* ]]; then
    current="/"
  else
    current="$PWD"
  fi
  IFS='/' read -ra components <<< "$input_file"
  for component in "${components[@]}"; do
    [[ -n "$component" && "$component" != "." ]] || continue
    current="${current%/}/$component"
    [[ ! -L "$current" ]] || return 0
  done
  return 1
}

outcome: an intent file reached only by traversing a symlinked directory or file is refused, not silently followed
notes: Consequence-class: safety — closes a symlink-traversal path around the intent-file safety check.

statement: An intent document is only valid if it contains exactly the eight required sections (Objective, Required Invariants, Approved Tradeoffs, Out Of Scope, State Transitions, Failure Windows, Negative Test Matrix, Validation Evidence), each appearing exactly once, in that exact order, and none left empty.

statement: An operator-supplied intent file is rejected if its path contains a newline or carriage return, or if it attempts path traversal (".." as a whole component or embedded), or if it does not exist.

source.quote:
if [[ -n "$input_file" ]]; then
    [[ "$input_file" != *$'\n'* && "$input_file" != *$'\r'* ]] || _die "intent path contains invalid characters"
    if [[ "$input_file" == ".." || "$input_file" == ../* || "$input_file" == */../* || "$input_file" == */.. ]]; then

statement: An operator-supplied intent file is rejected if it exceeds 65536 bytes, or if it contains control-character bytes other than tab and newline.

source.quote:
[[ "$(wc -c < "$input_file")" -le 65536 ]] || _die "intent file exceeds 65536 bytes"
    if LC_ALL=C od -An -tu1 "$input_file" | awk '
      { for (i = 1; i <= NF; i++) if (($i < 32 && $i != 9 && $i != 10) || $i == 127) bad = 1 }
      END { exit bad ? 0 : 1 }
    '; then
      _die "intent file contains unsupported control characters"
    fi

statement: A dispatch objective is rejected — requiring an explicit --intent-file instead — when it matches safety-sensitive or stateful keywords (auth, oauth, security, secrets, credentials, payments, databases, migrations, stateful, production, destructive, or persistent/state-transition phrasing).

## State Transitions

Standard-isolated path: no persistent or externally published state transition is authorized.

## Failure Windows

statement: Installing a prepared intent file into its target path is done by copying to a temp file in the target directory and then renaming it into place, never by writing the target path directly.

source.quote:
_sgt_intent_install() {
  local source_file="$1"
  local target_file="$2"
  local temporary_file="${target_file}.tmp.$$"

  if ! cp "$source_file" "$temporary_file"; then
    rm -f "$temporary_file"
    return 1
  fi
  mv "$temporary_file" "$target_file"
}

notes: Consequence-class: recovery — atomic publish avoids a half-written intent being read mid-write.

statement: sgt-td-memory binds every td call to the worktree its own fleet state record actually owns: a missing owned-worktree record, or a WORKTREE argument that resolves (via realpath) to a different path than the recorded one, fails closed with a diagnostic rather than trusting the caller's argument.

# reconciled, so it fails closed rather than trusting the argument.
owned_worktree="$(cat "$REPO_STATE/worktree" 2>/dev/null || true)"
if [[ -z "$owned_worktree" ]]; then
  _diagnose "unverified worktree for $ACTION on $TD_TASK: $REPO_STATE records no owned worktree"
  exit 1
fi
if [[ "$(_realpath "$owned_worktree")" != "$(_realpath "$WORKTREE")" ]]; then
  _diagnose "unverified worktree for $ACTION on $TD_TASK: $WORKTREE is not the owned worktree $owned_worktree"

    if ! worktree_root="$(git -C "$WORKTREE" rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null)" || \

      _diagnose "unverified worktree for $ACTION on $TD_TASK: $WORKTREE is not a git worktree"

    if ! head="$(git -C "$WORKTREE" rev-parse HEAD 2>/dev/null)" || [[ -z "$head" ]]; then
      _diagnose "git capture failed for $TD_TASK: cannot resolve HEAD in $WORKTREE"
      exit 1

    # line, so the empty value is rendered as the literal "detached" rather than
    # left blank.  The head above is the authoritative identity either way.
    [[ -n "$branch" ]] || branch="detached"

statement: The harness capability/registry check runs before any model/variant resolution work or durable state creation for the worker, so an unregistered harness fails immediately instead of after state has already been created.

source.quote:
# Capability gate, readiness probe, and launch invocation all come from the one
# registry in bin/_sgt-harness.sh.  Validation runs first, so a harness added to
# the accepted list without a readiness probe fails here instead of shipping and
# then hanging forever on an unsatisfiable readiness check.
harness="$(basename "$AGENT")"
# Registry check: validates the harness is in the accepted list before any
# model/variant work or state creation.
_sgt_harness_require_accepted "$harness" || exit 2

trigger: sgt-interactive-worker is launched with an agent/harness argument
outcome: an unaccepted harness is rejected before REPO_STATE or any launch bookkeeping exists

statement: The pinned model tuple lives in durable fleet state (not the ambient environment) so that a worker resumed by sgt-respond, sgt-recover, or sgt-wake runs the exact same pinned model as the original dispatch; a tuple the harness cannot honor is a terminal launch failure rather than silently falling back to an ambient default model.

source.quote:
# ── Pinned model tuple ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# The tuple lives in durable fleet state, so a worker resumed by sgt-respond,
# sgt-recover, or sgt-wake runs the same pinned model as the original dispatch.
# A tuple this harness cannot honor is a terminal failure: dropping the pin and
# inheriting the ambient default is exactly the defect this contract prevents.

AGENT_MODEL="$(cat "$REPO_STATE/agent_model" 2>/dev/null || true)"
AGENT_MODEL_SOURCE="$(cat "$REPO_STATE/agent_model_source" 2>/dev/null || true)"
[[ -n "$AGENT_MODEL" ]] || AGENT_MODEL="$SGT_AGENT_MODEL_UNPINNED"

trigger: a worker with a recorded agent_model is (re-)launched
outcome: the model actually run always matches the dispatch-time pin, or the worker fails loudly instead of silently substituting
notes: Consequence-class: identity — a pin established at creation must be honored exactly at every later resume, never silently substituted with an ambient default.

statement: When the resolved harness cannot honor the pinned model tuple, the worker writes the rejection reason to a diagnostic file and to both the fleet-state and worktree status sentinels as an explicit "failed: cannot honor pinned model tuple" before exiting, rather than launching with a substituted model.

source.quote:
# Called directly, not in a command substitution: the resolved base argv, model
# argv, and model environment are out-parameters that a subshell would discard.
# $REPO_STATE is passed so a variant transport that needs a generated harness
# definition materialises it in fleet state, never in the worktree under review.
if ! _sgt_resolve_agent_launch "$harness" "$AGENT_MODEL" "$REPO_STATE"; then
  _reject_reason="$(_sgt_agent_launch_reject_message "$harness" "$AGENT_MODEL" \
    "$SGT_LAUNCH_REJECT")"
  printf '%s\n' "$_reject_reason" > "$REPO_STATE/diagnostic"
  printf 'failed: cannot honor pinned model tuple %s\n' "$AGENT_MODEL" \
    > "$REPO_STATE/status"
  printf 'failed: cannot honor pinned model tuple %s\n' "$AGENT_MODEL" \
    > "$WORKTREE/.sergeant-status"
  echo "ERROR: $_reject_reason" >&2
  exit 2
fi

trigger: _sgt_resolve_agent_launch cannot honor the pinned model for this harness
outcome: the failure and its cause are durably recorded in three places before the process exits

statement: The launch record's launch_state field distinguishes intent from proof: it is written "intended" before the harness process is invoked and promoted to "confirmed" only once the harness is observably ready, so a harness that rejects the pin and exits never leaves evidence claiming the model actually ran; variant_verified is always recorded false because no supported harness reports back which variant it resolved.

source.quote:
# launch_state distinguishes intent from proof.  It is written as "intended"
# before the harness is executed and promoted to "confirmed" only once the
# harness reports itself ready (see _promote_launch_record), so a harness that
# rejects the pin and exits never leaves evidence claiming the model ran.
#
# provider_verified and variant_verified say whether the launch invocation itself
# proves that axis.  Both pinned model transports carry the provider explicitly,
# so provider_verified is true whenever a model is pinned and false only when
# nothing is.  variant_verified is always false today: the variant transport is
# genuine, but no supported harness reports back which variant it resolved, so
# claiming otherwise would be exactly the unevidenced assertion this contract
# exists to prevent.

trigger: a launch record is written and later promoted
outcome: launch evidence never overclaims a model/variant as verified beyond what was actually observed
notes: Consequence-class: identity — evidence of what actually ran is kept strictly separate from what was merely intended.

statement: The termination handler only sends a signal to the worker's own process group when this worker process actually leads that group; if it does not, it falls back to terminating only the worker shell and lets that shell's own EXIT path clean up, because a group it does not lead may contain processes it does not own.

source.quote:
# Only signal the group when this worker actually leads it.  A tmux pane command
  # is its own group leader, so pgid == worker pid.  If it is not, the group
  # contains processes this worker does not own and must not signal; fall back to
  # terminating just the worker shell and let its own EXIT path clean up.
  if [[ "$pgid" =~ ^[1-9][0-9]*$ && "$pgid" != "$$" ]]; then
    printf 'drain terminated the worker shell only: pid %s does not lead process group %s\n' \
      "$$" "$pgid" > "$REPO_STATE/diagnostic" 2>/dev/null || true
    pgid=""
  fi

trigger: _drain_terminate signals the process group
outcome: termination never signals processes outside the worker's own ownership just because they share an ambient process group id
notes: Consequence-class: safety — a destructive kill is gated on verifying the target group is actually led (owned) by this worker.

statement: Cooperative drain first performs a durable td handoff and finalizes the accepted action lease (from the agent's own proof, or explicitly recorded as still pending) before publishing the drained status and terminating; the drain path never invents a result, leaving status honestly as the nonterminal "drained" with any prior result file removed.

source.quote:
# _do_drain: publish durable drained state, then terminate.  Never returns.
_do_drain() {
  "$SCRIPT_DIR/sgt-td-memory" handoff "$REPO_STATE" "$WORKTREE" || true
  # A durable handoff settles the accepted action lease: either it is finalized
  # from the agent's own completion proof, or the drain is recorded as the reason
  # it stays outstanding.  Without this a cooperatively drained worker left the
  # lease pending forever and could never be resumed.
  _sgt_finalize_action_lease "$REPO_STATE" "$WORKTREE" "drain_handoff" || true
  printf 'drained\n' > "$WORKTREE/.sergeant-drained"
  printf 'drained\n' > "$WORKTREE/.sergeant-status"
  printf 'drained\n' > "$REPO_STATE/status"
  # Drain is not a way to discard unfinished work: no result is invented, and the
  # status stays the honest nonterminal `drained`.
  rm -f "$REPO_STATE/result"

trigger: an active drain is detected while the worker is running
outcome: a drained worker's outstanding lease is always settled and its handoff is durable before the process is torn down, and drain is never mistaken for completion
notes: Consequence-class: delivery/recovery — a durable record is published before a destructive/interrupting action (termination) begins.

statement: The termination watcher's double guard mirrors _finish's own rule: it only stops the Claude background session on status=done together with a non-empty result; a done status with an empty result is treated as an orphaned mission still in progress, never as completion.

source.quote:
# The double guard (terminal status AND non-empty result) mirrors _finish's own
# empty-result-means-orphaned handling and the required result-before-status write
# order (templates/worker-brief.md:131-132).  Do not fire on status=done with an
# empty result — that is an orphaned mission, not a completed one.
#

trigger: the Claude background session's status becomes done
outcome: a status flip to done with no result never triggers session termination as if the mission had genuinely completed
notes: Consequence-class: recovery — reclassifies an ambiguous terminal condition (done + empty result) rather than accepting it as clean completion.

statement: The termination watcher does not stop the background session on a done status with an empty result; it explicitly lets _finish handle that empty-result (orphaned) case whenever attach exits by other means.

source.quote:
fi
        # done with empty result: orphaned mission.  Do not stop; let _finish
        # handle the empty-result case when attach exits by other means.
        ;;

trigger: status is done with an empty .sergeant-result
outcome: the watcher does not race _finish's own orphaned-detection by terminating the session prematurely on an ambiguous done

statement: Any status matching failed:<reason> is treated as terminal by the termination watcher regardless of the result field's state, and stops the background session.

source.quote:
failed:*)
        # Any failed: <reason> value is terminal regardless of result state.
        "$AGENT" stop "$bg_id" 2>/dev/null || true
        return 0
        ;;
    esac

trigger: status becomes failed:<reason>
outcome: a failed mission's background session is stopped even though no result was ever expected

statement: When the bounded readiness gate's timeout elapses, the worker publishes a durable readiness_failed record (once) naming the notification, nonce, harness, and seconds waited.
trigger: a notification target's harness never becomes ready within SGT_HARNESS_READY_TIMEOUT
outcome: an unreachable readiness state is durably recorded exactly once rather than spinning silently forever
notes: Consequence-class: delivery/human-decision — a readiness gate with a stated, bounded timeout behavior instead of an unbounded fabricated wait.

statement: The readiness-timeout failure message explicitly states that no acknowledgement, acceptance, delivery, or action lease was fabricated and that the notification is still pending, directing the operator to confirm the harness renders a prompt and resume via sgt-respond.

source.quote:
printf 'evidence: %s\n' "$target_dir/readiness_failed"
    printf 'No acknowledgement, acceptance, delivery, or action lease was fabricated; the notification is still pending.\n'
    printf 'Confirm the harness can render an interactive prompt, then resume with sgt-respond.\n'
  } > "$WORKTREE/.sergeant-message"

trigger: the readiness gate times out and publishes its failure
outcome: the human sees an explicit non-fabrication guarantee and a concrete next action rather than an ambiguous stall
notes: Consequence-class: human-decision — states exactly what was NOT fabricated, alongside the concrete recoverable next step.

statement: On exit, the worker's _finish handler kills every background loop it started (notification delivery, progress watch, drain watch, termination watch) and stops any Claude background session as a ninth, in-process termination backstop independent of the eight external termination paths, so no background process leaks regardless of which exit path fired.

source.quote:
_finish() {
  local exit_code="$1" status
  trap - EXIT
  [[ -z "${notification_pid:-}" ]] || kill "$notification_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
  [[ -z "${watch_progress_pid:-}" ]] || kill "$watch_progress_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
  [[ -z "${watch_drain_pid:-}" ]] || kill "$watch_drain_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
  [[ -z "${watch_termination_pid:-}" ]] || kill "$watch_termination_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
  # Claude-specific backstop: stop the background session from _finish so no
  # background process leaks regardless of which exit path fires.  Idempotent
  # — safe to call after the termination watcher or _drain_terminate already
  # stopped it.  This is a ninth call site beyond the PRD's exhaustively-
  # enumerated eight EXTERNAL termination paths (Recovery Semantics) — _finish
  # runs inside this same worker process, as the terminal step of every exit
  # path including ones none of the eight external scripts observe (e.g. a
  # clean `done` exit with no external intervention at all), so it needs its
  # own backstop independent of them.  Harmless and idempotent either way; a
  # PRD revision should still record it as a ninth site rather than leave it
  # implicit.
  _sgt_claude_stop_bg_session "$REPO_STATE"

trigger: the worker process is exiting for any reason
outcome: every background loop and the Claude background session are stopped on every exit path, including a clean completion no external script observes
notes: Consequence-class: delivery/recovery — guarantees cleanup happens exactly once across every possible exit path, not zero times on an unobserved path.

statement: At the worker's exit boundary, the accepted action lease is always settled — finalized from the agent's own completion proof, or explicitly recorded as pending with the exit reason — covering every terminal status (done, failed, drained, needs_input, blocked, waiting, orphaned) so no branch can exit leaving the lease silently outstanding.

source.quote:
# Settle the accepted action lease at the exit boundary, before any branch can
  # return.  This covers done, failed, drained, needs_input, blocked, waiting and
  # orphaned alike: the lease is either finalized from the agent's own completion
  # proof or explicitly recorded as pending with the exit reason.  No branch may
  # exit leaving it silently outstanding.  The background loops are already dead,
  # so there is no competing writer.
  _sgt_finalize_action_lease "$REPO_STATE" "$WORKTREE" "worker_exit:$status" || true

trigger: the worker process reaches its exit trap
outcome: an accepted action lease is never left in limbo after the worker process is gone
notes: Consequence-class: delivery — a single finalizer every exit path funnels through before the process ends.

statement: On exit, a status of done together with an empty .sergeant-result is downgraded to orphaned rather than accepted as a completed mission.

source.quote:
case "$status" in
    done)
      if [[ ! -s "$WORKTREE/.sergeant-result" ]]; then
        status="orphaned"
      fi
      ;;

trigger: the worker's final status is done but .sergeant-result is empty
outcome: an unsubstantiated "done" is never reported to the coordinator as a genuine completion
notes: Consequence-class: recovery — reclassifies an ambiguous terminal condition (empty result) as orphaned rather than accepting it as clean done.

statement: When a worker exits orphaned, _finish inspects git log above the dispatch base (or, absent that record, commits not on the upstream tracking branch) and records in the diagnostic whether real committed work exists, so the coordinator can distinguish a clean orphan from an interrupted worker with real work needing reconciliation before re-dispatch.

source.quote:
if [[ "$status" == "orphaned" ]]; then
    printf 'orphaned\n' > "$WORKTREE/.sergeant-status"
    printf 'orphaned\n' > "$REPO_STATE/status"
    # Check for committed work above the dispatch base so the coordinator can
    # distinguish a clean orphan (nothing committed) from an interrupted fallback
    # that has real work.  Uses initial_sha written by sgt-dispatch at dispatch
    # time; falls back to checking for commits not on any remote.
    local _initial_sha _committed_log
    _initial_sha="$(cat "$REPO_STATE/initial_sha" 2>/dev/null || true)"
    _committed_log=""
    if command -v git >/dev/null 2>&1 && [[ -d "$WORKTREE" ]]; then
      if [[ -n "$_initial_sha" ]]; then
        _committed_log="$(git -C "$WORKTREE" log --oneline "${_initial_sha}..HEAD" 2>/dev/null || true)"
      else
        # Fallback for fleet states predating initial_sha: show commits not in
        # the upstream tracking branch (if configured).
        _committed_log="$(git -C "$WORKTREE" log --oneline HEAD --not "@{u}" 2>/dev/null || true)"
      fi
    fi
    {
      printf 'reason: interactive %s session exited before terminal completion\n' "$harness"
      printf 'exit code: %s\n' "$exit_code"
      if [[ -n "$_committed_log" ]]; then
        printf 'committed-work-present: %d commit(s) above base; reconcile before re-dispatch\n' \
          "$(printf '%s\n' "$_committed_log" | wc -l | tr -d ' ')"
        printf '%s\n' "$_committed_log"
      fi
    } > "$REPO_STATE/diagnostic"
    "$SCRIPT_DIR/sgt-td-memory" handoff "$REPO_STATE" "$WORKTREE" || true

trigger: the worker's terminal status resolves to orphaned
outcome: the diagnostic distinguishes "nothing committed, safe to re-dispatch" from "committed work above base, reconcile before re-dispatch"
notes: Consequence-class: human-decision — surfaces the fact a human must reconcile before re-dispatch rather than silently discarding it.

statement: When the agent itself publishes a completion proof for a notification, the worker settles the accepted action lease through the one shared finalizer (which re-verifies identity, lease, and proof under the response lock) rather than a second, separately-maintained inline implementation.

source.quote:
# The agent published its own completion proof for this turn.  Settle the
      # lease through the one shared finalizer rather than a second inline
      # implementation; it takes the response lock, re-verifies identity, lease
      # and proof under it, and records the outcome either way.
      if [[ "$(cat "$complete_path" 2>/dev/null || true)" == "$ack_token" &&
            ! -f "$target_dir/completed" ]]; then
        _sgt_finalize_action_lease "$REPO_STATE" "$WORKTREE" "notification_complete" || true
      fi

trigger: the agent writes its own completion proof for a delivered notification
outcome: lease settlement for agent-initiated completion goes through the exact same verified path as every other settlement, avoiding a second implementation that could diverge

statement: When the notification delivery loop is about to accept a notification target, it re-checks whether an action lease already exists for a different nonce and refuses to overwrite it; only when no lease exists does it atomically claim the lease for the current nonce via mktemp+mv.
trigger: the acceptance path is about to claim the action lease for a notification target
outcome: at most one nonce ever holds the action lease for a given notification — a second target cannot silently steal or duplicate acceptance
notes: Consequence-class: delivery — a lease ensures the accepted action happens through exactly one target, not concurrently through two.

statement: The Claude harness pre-flight capability gate verifies the resolved $AGENT binary itself is present, resolved through the harness path this worker was invoked with (not a hardcoded literal claude) so a fake-CLI test can substitute its own binary the same way every other harness-launch test does.

source.quote:
if [[ "$harness" == "claude" ]]; then
  # Capability gate: verify every required claude subcommand is available.
  # Resolved through $AGENT (the harness path this worker was invoked with),
  # not a hardcoded literal `claude`, so a fake-CLI test can substitute its own
  # binary the same way every other harness-launch test in this tree already
  # does.  The bypass-permissions disclaimer is documented as a required
  # one-time per-machine/account setup step (PRD CH-7): run
  # `claude --dangerously-skip-permissions` interactively once per machine/
  # account before dispatching a Claude worker; it cannot be checked here
  # because its exact refusal text and exit code were not independently
  # measured on a fresh machine.
  command -v "$AGENT" >/dev/null 2>&1 || {
    printf 'failed: claude command not found\n' > "$REPO_STATE/status"
    printf 'failed: claude command not found\n' > "$WORKTREE/.sergeant-status"
    echo "ERROR: claude command not found; install Claude Code ≥ 2.1.220" >&2
    exit 2
  }

trigger: the harness resolved for this worker is claude
outcome: a missing claude binary fails the launch immediately with an actionable version-floor message rather than failing deep inside the launch sequence

statement: Before spending a real API call, the Claude harness pre-flight rejects any model value that does not match a bare known alias (sonnet/opus/haiku/fable) or a full claude-<family>-<version> ID, as defence-in-depth against a bypass of the normal tuple-parsing path.

source.quote:
# Pre-flight model regex: reject any model value that is not a bare alias
  # or a full claude-<family>-<version> ID before spending a real API call.
  # The provider segment was already stripped by _sgt_resolve_agent_launch
  # (argv-bare transport, provider_scope=anthropic), so the value reaching this
  # check is the model ID only.  The regex is still load-bearing as defence-in-
  # depth against a bypass of the normal tuple-parsing path.
  _SGT_CLAUDE_MODEL_RE='^(sonnet|opus|haiku|fable|claude-[a-z][a-z0-9]*-[0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]*)$'
  if [[ "${#SGT_LAUNCH_MODEL_ARGV[@]}" -ge 2 ]]; then
    # Bash 3.2 has no negative array subscript ([-1]); compute the last index
    # explicitly, matching the version floor _sgt-bash-version.sh enforces.
    _sgt_last_idx=$(( ${#SGT_LAUNCH_MODEL_ARGV[@]} - 1 ))
    _sgt_model_val="${SGT_LAUNCH_MODEL_ARGV[$_sgt_last_idx]}"
    unset _sgt_last_idx
    if [[ ! "$_sgt_model_val" =~ $_SGT_CLAUDE_MODEL_RE ]]; then
      printf 'failed: claude model pin rejected by pre-flight check: %s\n' \
        "$_sgt_model_val" > "$REPO_STATE/diagnostic"
      printf 'failed: claude model pin rejected: %s\n' "$_sgt_model_val" \
        > "$REPO_STATE/status"
      printf 'failed: claude model pin rejected: %s\n' "$_sgt_model_val" \
        > "$WORKTREE/.sergeant-status"
      echo "ERROR: claude model pin rejected by pre-flight check: $_sgt_model_val" >&2
      exit 2
    fi
    unset _sgt_model_val
  fi

trigger: SGT_LAUNCH_MODEL_ARGV carries a pinned model for the claude harness
outcome: an obviously-invalid model value is rejected before any API call is made, with the failure recorded in three places
notes: Consequence-class: identity/safety — a pinned model identity is validated before the harness is trusted to honor it.

statement: The Claude background session ID returned by claude --bg is validated at capture time against the exact same charset regex every one of the nine termination-path backstops uses to resolve it; a malformed ID fails the launch immediately rather than being persisted and silently defeating every one of those backstops later.

source.quote:
# Fail closed on a malformed background ID here, at capture time, rather
  # than relying on _sgt_claude_bg_id_and_bin's read-side charset check to
  # coincidentally match whatever the CLI happened to emit.  Every one of the
  # nine termination-path backstops resolves the id through that same regex
  # (bin/_sgt-drain.sh), so an id outside this shape would otherwise get
  # persisted and later silently defeat every one of those backstops.
  if [[ ! "$_SGT_CLAUDE_BG_ID" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]*$ ]]; then
    printf 'failed: claude --bg returned malformed background ID: %s\n' \
      "$_SGT_CLAUDE_BG_ID" > "$REPO_STATE/status"
    printf 'failed: claude --bg returned malformed background ID: %s\n' \
      "$_SGT_CLAUDE_BG_ID" > "$WORKTREE/.sergeant-status"
    echo "ERROR: claude --bg returned malformed background ID: $_SGT_CLAUDE_BG_ID" >&2
    exit 2
  fi

trigger: claude --bg returns a background ID
outcome: a malformed background ID can never be persisted into fleet state where every termination backstop assumes the well-formed shape
notes: Consequence-class: safety/recovery — fail-closed check protecting nine separate termination-path recovery mechanisms from a malformed identity.

statement: The Claude background ID is persisted to fleet state immediately after capture, before the (potentially multi-second) post-launch liveness check loop runs, so a worker process death during that window cannot leave a genuinely live background session with no recorded identity anywhere.

source.quote:
# Persist the background ID immediately, before the liveness check loop
  # below (which can take several real seconds against a genuine API call,
  # not just its bounded worst case) — not after it.  A worker process death
  # during that window would otherwise leave a genuinely live background
  # session with no recorded identity anywhere, so none of the nine
  # termination-path backstops could ever find and stop it.  claude_session_id
  # is not yet known at this point; the second _record_worker_identity call
  # after the liveness loop adds it once the liveness check has parsed it.
  _record_worker_identity

trigger: claude --bg has returned a validated background ID
outcome: every one of the nine termination-path backstops can find and stop the session even if the worker process dies during the liveness check
notes: Consequence-class: recovery — a durable record is published before an interruptible window (the liveness poll) rather than after it.

statement: During the bounded post-launch liveness poll, if the Claude background session's reported state reaches "failed", the launch is treated as a terminal failure (status/sentinel written, process exits) rather than continuing to poll or attaching anyway.

source.quote:
if [[ "$_sgt_claude_state" == "failed" ]]; then
          printf 'failed: claude background session failed after launch: id=%s\n' \
            "$_SGT_CLAUDE_BG_ID" > "$REPO_STATE/status"
          printf 'failed: claude background session failed after launch: id=%s\n' \
            "$_SGT_CLAUDE_BG_ID" > "$WORKTREE/.sergeant-status"
          echo "ERROR: claude background session failed post-launch: $_SGT_CLAUDE_BG_ID" >&2
          exit 2
        fi
        [[ "$_sgt_claude_state" != "" ]] && break

trigger: the background session's polled state is "failed" within the liveness window
outcome: a session that failed immediately after launch is never attached to as if it were healthy

statement: Respawn/reattach after an attach exit is only ever considered while .sergeant-status is still the unchanged in_progress it started at; any other value (done, failed:*, drained, orphaned, or a cooperative needs_input/blocked/waiting gate the agent itself published) is treated as the agent or an existing mechanism having already decided the outcome, so attach exiting afterward is expected, not an unexpected death.

source.quote:
# Respawn/reattach is only ever considered while .sergeant-status is still
    # the unchanged "in_progress" it started at: any OTHER value — done,
    # failed:*, drained, orphaned, or a cooperative nonterminal gate the agent
    # itself published (needs_input, blocked, waiting) — means the agent or an
    # existing mechanism already decided how this turn ends, and attach
    # exiting afterward is the expected, not the unexpected, case.  Matching a
    # fixed list of "terminal-looking" values here previously missed
    # needs_input/blocked/waiting, which made a legitimate cooperative gate
    # look like an unexpected death and triggered a spurious re-attach.
    if [[ "$_sgt_attach_status" != "in_progress" ]]; then
      break
    fi

trigger: the blocking claude attach call exits
outcome: a legitimate cooperative gate (needs_input/blocked/waiting) is never mistaken for an unexpected death and spuriously re-attached
notes: Consequence-class: recovery — a prior version's fixed terminal-value list missed cooperative gates and mis-triggered a spurious re-attach; the rule now checks specifically for the unchanged starting state.

statement: When attach exits while status is still in_progress, the worker distinguishes a genuinely dead background session (state=stopped, requiring respawn before re-attach to restore the same session/conversation) from a session that never died (state=working/blocked, requiring only a direct re-attach with no respawn).

source.quote:
case "$_sgt_session_state" in
      stopped)
        # Unexpected death: respawn to restore the session (same sessionId,
        # conversation intact), then clear the pane and re-attach.
        if "$AGENT" respawn "$_SGT_CLAUDE_BG_ID" 2>/dev/null; then
          _sgt_reattach
          continue
        fi
        ;;
      working|blocked)
        # The session never died; only the attach connection did.  Re-attach
        # directly — no respawn needed, since nothing needs restoring.
        _sgt_reattach
        continue
        ;;
    esac

trigger: attach exits non-terminally and the background session state is queried
outcome: a still-live session is never respawned unnecessarily, and a genuinely dead session is always restored via respawn before reattaching
notes: Consequence-class: identity/recovery — the same underlying session identity is preserved across an unexpected attach-connection loss.

statement: After the main Claude invocation exits, if a model was pinned, the worker scans the session transcript for the substitution warning line ("is restricted by your organization's settings... Using <Y> instead") and, if found, records a durable model_substitution_warning in fleet state and prints a WARNING — since neither the pre-flight regex nor the liveness check can catch a valid-but-unentitled model alias that Claude silently substitutes without any failed state or nonzero exit code.

source.quote:
# ── Transcript substitution-warning scan ────────────────────────────────────
# Neither the pre-flight regex nor the post-launch liveness check catches a
# valid model alias the account is not entitled to: Claude silently substitutes
# another model and completes the mission successfully, with no failed state and
# no non-zero exit code.  The only signal is a transcript line:
#   Model "<X>" is restricted by your organization's settings. Using <Y> instead.
# A pinned model is "honored" only when this scan confirms the line's absence.
# This check runs after the attach exits to avoid blocking the mission itself;
# it records a diagnostic but does not change the mission's terminal status.
if [[ "$harness" == "claude" && -n "$_SGT_CLAUDE_BG_ID" && \
      "$_SGT_CLAUDE_MODEL_PINNED" == "true" ]] && \
   command -v "$AGENT" >/dev/null 2>&1 && command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  _sgt_transcript="$("$AGENT" agents --json 2>/dev/null | \
    jq -r ".[] | select(.id == \"$_SGT_CLAUDE_BG_ID\") | .transcript // \"\"" \
    2>/dev/null || true)"
  if printf '%s' "$_sgt_transcript" | \
      grep -qiF 'is restricted by your organization' 2>/dev/null; then
    _sgt_subst_warning="model substitution warning detected in Claude transcript for $_SGT_CLAUDE_BG_ID: pinned model may not have been honored"

trigger: the claude attach invocation has exited and a model was pinned for this session
outcome: a silent model substitution the account was never entitled to is durably surfaced even though the mission itself completed successfully
notes: Consequence-class: identity — a pinned model's actual identity is verified after the fact via transcript evidence, since no other signal catches this substitution class.

statement: The model-substitution warning is written to its own dedicated file rather than $REPO_STATE/diagnostic, because _finish unconditionally clears the shared diagnostic file on every non-orphaned exit (including this successful-mission path), which would otherwise erase the warning before anything could read it.

source.quote:
_sgt_subst_warning="model substitution warning detected in Claude transcript for $_SGT_CLAUDE_BG_ID: pinned model may not have been honored"
    # A dedicated file, not $REPO_STATE/diagnostic: _finish unconditionally
    # clears the shared diagnostic file on every non-orphaned exit (including
    # the success path this scan runs on), so writing there would erase the
    # warning before anything could read it.  This finding must survive a
    # successful mission's own cleanup.
    printf '%s\n' "$_sgt_subst_warning" >> "$REPO_STATE/model_substitution_warning"
    printf 'WARNING: %s\n' "$_sgt_subst_warning" >&2

trigger: a model-substitution warning is detected after a successful mission
outcome: the substitution finding survives the successful mission's own diagnostic cleanup instead of being silently erased
notes: Consequence-class: delivery — ensures a finding is durably delivered despite an unrelated cleanup step that would otherwise destroy it.

statement: Accepting a coordinator ownership handover from a previously unseen pane requires proving that this process genuinely lives inside that pane's process tree (walking up to 64 ppid hops); merely exporting the TMUX_PANE variable cannot satisfy this proof.

source.quote:
# Prove this process really lives inside <pane-pid>'s process tree. A caller that
# merely exports TMUX_PANE cannot satisfy this, which is what makes accepting an
# ownership handover from a previously unseen pane safe.
_coordinator_runs_in_pane() {
  local target="$1" pid="$$" hops=0
  [[ "$target" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || return 1
  while [[ "$hops" -lt 64 ]]; do
    [[ "$pid" != "$target" ]] || return 0
    [[ "$pid" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && "$pid" -gt 1 ]] || return 1
    pid="$(ps -o ppid= -p "$pid" 2>/dev/null | tr -d '[:space:]')"
    hops=$((hops + 1))
  done
  return 1
}

trigger: a pane claims coordinator ownership of a validation task
outcome: ownership can only be claimed by a process that is actually a descendant of the claiming pane, not by any process that merely sets an environment variable
notes: Consequence-class: identity — process-tree ancestry, not a spoofable environment variable, is what makes accepting a handover safe.

statement: Claiming coordinator ownership determines its handover reason by checking, in order: whether the prior owner explicitly released ownership (released-by-owner); otherwise refusing outright if the prior owner's pane is still live and has not released; otherwise recording whether the prior pane still exists but was recycled to a different identity, or is simply gone.

source.quote:
if [[ -n "$released" && "$released" == "$RECORDED_PRIMARY_IDENTITY" ]]; then
    reason="released-by-owner"
  elif $PRIMARY_OWNER_IS_LIVE; then
    _die "Refusing handover: dispatching coordinator pane $PRIMARY_PANE_ID" \
      "is still live and has not released ownership"
  elif $PRIMARY_PANE_PRESENT; then
    reason="dispatching-pane-recycled"
  else
    reason="dispatching-pane-dead"
  fi

trigger: a pane attempts --claim-ownership of a validation task
outcome: a live, non-releasing prior owner can never be silently displaced; every accepted claim records a specific, auditable reason
notes: Consequence-class: safety/identity — refuses to override a still-live, non-consenting owner.

statement: --release-ownership is an ownership-only operation: it never inspects worker readiness and never launches a validation run, and it can only be performed by the pane currently recorded as the owner (both its tmux pane ID and its recorded identity must match exactly).

source.quote:
if $RELEASE_OWNERSHIP; then
  _require_tmux
  _resolve_coordinator_ownership
  [[ "$TMUX_PANE" == "$PRIMARY_PANE_ID" && \
    "$RECORDED_PRIMARY_IDENTITY" == "$CURRENT_PANE_IDENTITY" ]] || \
    _die "Only the recorded coordinator pane can release ownership;" \
      "task $TASK_ID is owned by $PRIMARY_PANE_ID"
  _sgt_replace_owned_file "$PRIMARY_PANE_RELEASED_RECORD" "$RECORDED_PRIMARY_IDENTITY" || \
    _die "Failed to record coordinator ownership release"
  printf 'Coordinator ownership of %s released by pane %s.\n' "$TASK_ID" "$TMUX_PANE"
  exit 0

trigger: sgt-validate --release-ownership is invoked
outcome: ownership release is a pure, narrowly-scoped operation that cannot be triggered by any pane other than the actual current owner, and never accidentally triggers a validation launch
notes: Consequence-class: human-decision/identity — only the verified current owner may relinquish an authorization, and releasing never has launch side effects.

statement: Before proceeding with any validation launch, the canonical intent revision recorded at the fleet, repo-state, and worktree levels must all match (via _sgt_intent_revision_matches); a mismatch is fatal, requiring an audited human decision or a new revision rather than proceeding on stale or divergent intent.

source.quote:
_sgt_intent_revision_matches "$TASK_STATE" "$REPO_STATE" "$WORKTREE" || \
  _die "canonical intent revision mismatch; audited human decision/new revision required"

trigger: sgt-validate is invoked to launch validation
outcome: validation never runs against an intent whose recorded revision has silently diverged across fleet/repo/worktree state
notes: Consequence-class: identity — the same intent identity is re-verified at this later re-entry point, not assumed to still hold.

statement: Validation only launches if all three review axes recorded on the validation-ready marker (standards, spec, readiness) are exactly "passed"; any other value fails with a message naming the specific axis and its actual recorded value.

source.quote:
for _REVIEW_AXIS in standards:"$STANDARDS_REVIEW" spec:"$SPEC_REVIEW" \
  readiness:"$READINESS_REVIEW"; do
  [[ "${_REVIEW_AXIS#*:}" == "passed" ]] || \
    _die "validation-ready marker records ${_REVIEW_AXIS%%:*}_review=${_REVIEW_AXIS#*:}," \
      "but validation requires passed"
done

trigger: sgt-validate reads the worktree's .sergeant-validation-ready marker
outcome: validation is refused unless every required review axis has independently recorded a pass, and the failure names exactly which axis did not
notes: Consequence-class: human-decision — a gate that requires three independent prior sign-offs before a further destructive/consequential step (validation launch) proceeds.

statement: The worker's code tree must be clean (per _sgt_worktree_is_validation_clean) before a validation snapshot is taken; a dirty tree fails validation launch outright.

source.quote:
_sgt_worktree_is_validation_clean "$WORKTREE" || \
  _die "Worker code tree must be clean before validation snapshot"

trigger: sgt-validate is about to snapshot the worktree for isolated validation
outcome: validation never runs against an uncommitted or otherwise dirty working tree

statement: The intent transport (private intent-file vs. consented argv) is resolved and validated before any validation run, marker, or state change exists, specifically so that an incompatible no-mistakes build cannot record a failed run.

source.quote:
# Probe the intent transport before any validation run, marker, or state change
# exists, so an incompatible no-mistakes build cannot record a failed run.
set +e
INTENT_TRANSPORT="$(_sgt_resolve_intent_transport "$ALLOW_ARGV_INTENT")"
INTENT_TRANSPORT_STATUS=$?
set -e
[[ "$INTENT_TRANSPORT_STATUS" -eq 0 ]] || \
  _die "$(_sgt_intent_transport_diagnostic "$INTENT_TRANSPORT_STATUS")"

trigger: sgt-validate begins launching a validation run
outcome: a transport-incapable no-mistakes build is caught before any durable validation state is created, not mid-launch

statement: For a worker whose recorded status is not done or needs_input (i.e. it is expected to still be running), validation launch requires the recorded worker pane identity to still match a live pane; a done or needs_input worker is exempt from this check since its pane is expected to already be dead.

source.quote:
_WORKER_STATUS="$(cat "$REPO_STATE/status" 2>/dev/null || true)"
# A done or needs_input worker has exited cleanly; its pane will be dead.
# Allow validation to proceed without requiring a live pane for terminal workers.
if [[ "$_WORKER_STATUS" != "done" && "$_WORKER_STATUS" != "needs_input" ]]; then
  if [[ -z "$PANE" ]] || ! _sgt_pane_identity_matches "$PANE" "$REPO_STATE"; then
    _die "Recorded worker pane identity does not match"
  fi
fi

trigger: sgt-validate checks the worker's pane before launching validation
outcome: a validation run is never launched believing a still-running worker's pane is intact when it is not, while a cleanly-terminated worker's expectedly-dead pane does not spuriously block validation
notes: Consequence-class: identity — worker pane identity is re-verified at this later re-entry, conditioned on the worker's own recorded terminal state.

statement: The validation launch lock can be recovered from a stale prior owner only if that owner's PID is a genuine number, its recorded coordinator and purpose exactly match the current claimant's, and — critically — if that PID is still alive, its process start time must differ from the one recorded at lock time (proving PID reuse, not the same still-running holder) before the lock is treated as abandoned.

source.quote:
_recover_validation_lock() {
  local identity owner_pid owner_start owner_coordinator owner_purpose current_start
  [[ -f "$VALIDATION_LAUNCH_LOCK" && ! -L "$VALIDATION_LAUNCH_LOCK" ]] || return 1
  [[ "$(wc -l < "$VALIDATION_LAUNCH_LOCK")" -eq 4 ]] || return 1
  owner_pid="$(_validation_lock_field pid "$VALIDATION_LAUNCH_LOCK")" || return 1
  owner_start="$(_validation_lock_field start "$VALIDATION_LAUNCH_LOCK")" || return 1
  owner_coordinator="$(_validation_lock_field coordinator "$VALIDATION_LAUNCH_LOCK")" || return 1
  owner_purpose="$(_validation_lock_field purpose "$VALIDATION_LAUNCH_LOCK")" || return 1
  [[ "$owner_pid" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && "$owner_coordinator" == "$LOCK_COORDINATOR" && \
    "$owner_purpose" == "$LOCK_PURPOSE" ]] || return 1
  identity="$(_validation_path_identity "$VALIDATION_LAUNCH_LOCK")" || return 1
  if kill -0 "$owner_pid" 2>/dev/null; then
    current_start="$(_validation_process_start "$owner_pid" || true)"
    [[ -n "$current_start" && "$current_start" != "$owner_start" ]] || return 1
  fi

trigger: acquiring the validation launch lock finds an existing lock file
outcome: a lock is never reclaimed out from under its genuine still-running owner; only a provably-reused PID (different process start time) or a dead PID allows recovery
notes: Consequence-class: identity/safety — a PID-reuse check gates lock reclamation, not merely "a process currently exists at this PID".

statement: Resetting retryable validation state after a prior exit refuses to proceed if the recorded owner PID is still alive with the same recorded start time and process group (validation processes are still genuinely running), or if pgrep finds any live descendant process still in the recorded process group even after the primary PID is confirmed dead.

source.quote:
if kill -0 "$recorded_pid" 2>/dev/null; then
    current_start="$(_validation_process_start "$recorded_pid" || true)"
    [[ "$current_start" == "$recorded_start" ]] || \
      _die "Validation owner PID was reused; refusing retry reset: $recorded_pid"
    current_pgid="$(ps -o pgid= -p "$recorded_pid" 2>/dev/null | tr -d ' ' || true)"
    [[ "$current_pgid" == "$recorded_pgid" ]] || \
      _die "Validation owner process group changed; refusing retry reset: $recorded_pid"
    _die "Validation processes are still running in process group $recorded_pgid"
  fi
  live_pids="$(pgrep -g "$recorded_pgid" 2>/dev/null || true)"
  [[ -z "$live_pids" ]] || \
    _die "Validation pane disappeared with unverified detached descendants in process group $recorded_pgid"

trigger: sgt-validate is retried after a prior validation exit
outcome: a retry can never reset state while genuinely live validation processes, primary or unverified detached descendants, remain running
notes: Consequence-class: safety/recovery — a destructive reset is gated on proving no live process still holds the prior state.

statement: Before removing the isolated validation code snapshot during a retry reset, sgt-validate requires lsof to be installed and uses it to verify no process still has any file inside the snapshot open; any such process aborts the reset with the offending PIDs named.

source.quote:
command -v lsof >/dev/null 2>&1 || _die "lsof is required to verify validation snapshot cleanup"
  cwd_pids="$(lsof -t +D "$checkout" 2>/dev/null || true)"
  [[ -z "$cwd_pids" ]] || \
    _die "Processes still have $checkout open during retry reset: $(tr '\n' ' ' <<< "$cwd_pids")"

trigger: sgt-validate is about to remove a finished validation snapshot
outcome: a validation checkout with a still-open file handle is never removed out from under a live process
notes: Consequence-class: safety — a destructive removal is gated on an independent open-handle check, not merely process-liveness.

statement: The isolated validation code snapshot is created as a --shared --no-checkout clone of the source worktree's root, then hard-checked-out to exactly the reviewed HEAD; the launch fails outright if the resulting HEAD or tree cleanliness does not match what was reviewed.

source.quote:
git clone --shared --no-checkout "$SOURCE_ROOT" "$VALIDATION_WORKTREE" >/dev/null 2>&1 || \
  _die "Failed to create isolated validation code snapshot"
git -C "$VALIDATION_WORKTREE" checkout -q -B "$SOURCE_BRANCH" "$CURRENT_HEAD" || \
  _die "Failed to create isolated validation code snapshot"

trigger: sgt-validate creates the isolated validation snapshot
outcome: the code actually validated is provably the exact reviewed commit, never a snapshot that silently drifted during creation
notes: Consequence-class: identity — the reviewed HEAD identity is enforced exactly onto the isolated snapshot, not merely approximated.

statement: A validation checkout owner token (combining the lock purpose, lock identity, and the reviewed HEAD) is written into the isolated snapshot's own .git directory immediately after creation, binding that specific checkout to this specific launch.

source.quote:
VALIDATION_OWNER="$LOCK_PURPOSE|$VALIDATION_LOCK_IDENTITY|$CURRENT_HEAD"
(umask 077; set -C; printf '%s\n' "$VALIDATION_OWNER" > \
  "$VALIDATION_GIT_DIR/sergeant-validation-owner") 2>/dev/null || \
  _die "Failed to persist validation checkout owner"

trigger: the isolated validation snapshot's git directory is created
outcome: a later retry-reset or rollback can verify a snapshot is really the one this launch created, not a namesake reused by coincidence
notes: Consequence-class: identity.

statement: The --skip value is interpolated unquoted into the constructed validation-worker launch command deliberately, because printf %q would escape a comma (a brace-expansion special character) in a way that would not match the literally-recorded pane_start_command later compared against it; SKIP is independently constrained to a safe [a-z]+(,[a-z]+)* pattern beforehand.

source.quote:
# SKIP stays unquoted: printf %q escapes a comma (brace-expansion special), and
# the recorded pane_start_command is compared literally. SKIP is already
# constrained to ^[a-z]+(,[a-z]+)*$, and an empty SKIP simply omits the argument.
printf -v VALIDATION_COMMAND '%q %q %q %q %q %s' \
  "$SCRIPT_DIR/sgt-validation-worker" "$REPO_STATE" "$VALIDATION_WORKTREE" \
  "$EXPECTED_REVISION" "$INTENT_TRANSPORT" "$SKIP"

trigger: the validation-worker launch command is assembled
outcome: the recorded pane_start_command used for later identity comparison stays byte-for-byte consistent with what was actually launched

statement: If splitting a new validation pane beside the worker's own pane fails and the worker's own status is done (its pane expectedly already dead), sgt-validate falls back to opening a new tmux window instead, rather than failing the validation launch outright.

source.quote:
# If the worker pane is dead (done workers exit cleanly), fall back to a new window.
if [[ "$SPLIT_STATUS" -ne 0 && "$_WORKER_STATUS" == "done" ]]; then
  SPLIT_IDENTITY="$(tmux new-window -P -F "$PANE_FORMAT" \
    -n "validation-${REPO}-${TASK_ID}" \
    -c "$VALIDATION_WORKTREE" "$VALIDATION_COMMAND" 2>/dev/null)"
  SPLIT_STATUS=$?
fi

trigger: tmux split-window against the worker's pane fails
outcome: validation of an already-completed worker is not blocked merely because that worker's own pane is gone

statement: The intent transport actually used for a validation run (intent-file or consented argv) is recorded to an append-only audit log as the last publication step of a committed launch; the comment notes over-recording is the conservative direction for this privacy-relevant decision even though a failure at this step still rolls the whole launch back.

source.quote:
# Recorded as the last publication step: the log is append-only, so a failure here
# still rolls the launch back and may leave the line behind. Over-recording an
# intent-transport decision is the conservative direction for a privacy audit.
printf -v TRANSPORT_AUDIT_LINE 'at=%s\ttransport=%s\trepo=%s\thead=%s\tintent_revision=%s' \
  "$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)" "$INTENT_TRANSPORT" "$REPO" "$CURRENT_HEAD" \
  "$EXPECTED_REVISION"
_append_owned_audit_line "$VALIDATION_TRANSPORT_LOG" "$TRANSPORT_AUDIT_LINE" || \
  _die "Failed to record the validation intent transport audit"

trigger: a validation launch reaches its final commit step
outcome: a consented argv-transport run stays durably auditable after the fact, and the log favors over- rather than under-recording
notes: Consequence-class: human-decision — a privacy-sensitive consent decision is durably audited.

statement: Rollback of a failed or aborted validation launch removes an owned path (or restores a backed-up prior window/stage state) only if that path's captured identity (device+inode+birthtime, plus content checksum for files) still matches what was recorded when this launch owned it, so a path that was replaced by something else in the meantime is left untouched rather than deleted or overwritten.

source.quote:
if ! $checkout_delete_failed; then
    _validation_remove_owned_paths || cleanup_failed=true
  fi
  if $WINDOW_STATE_OWNED && ! _validation_path_exists "$REPO_STATE/window_name" && \
    [[ "$(_validation_path_identity "$WINDOW_BACKUP" || true)" == "$OLD_WINDOW_IDENTITY" ]]; then
    if ! ln "$WINDOW_BACKUP" "$REPO_STATE/window_name" 2>/dev/null || \
      ! rm -f "$WINDOW_BACKUP"; then
      printf 'ERROR: rollback could not restore prior window state\n' >&2
      cleanup_failed=true

trigger: a validation launch fails or aborts before committing
outcome: rollback never deletes or clobbers a path that has since been reused for something unrelated to this launch, even though the path name is the same
notes: Consequence-class: safety — a destructive rollback (delete/restore) is gated on an identity re-check, not merely a path-name match.

statement: Every durable state write during validation launch (_validation_write_owned) follows the same pattern: create a private temp candidate file, verify its identity is unchanged immediately after writing content, hard-link it into its final path, and record ownership of each intermediate path at each step, so the launch can distinguish and reliably roll back exactly what it created.

source.quote:
_validation_write_owned() {
  local path="$1" value="$2" transition="${3:-state}" keep="${4:-false}"
  local candidate identity
  candidate="${path}.candidate.$$.$RANDOM.$RANDOM"
  (umask 077; set -C; : > "$candidate") 2>/dev/null || return 1
  _validation_record_owned_path "$candidate" || return 1
  _validation_transition "${transition}-temp" || return 1
  identity="$(_validation_object_identity "$candidate")" || return 1
  printf '%s\n' "$value" > "$candidate" || return 1
  [[ "$(_validation_object_identity "$candidate" || true)" == "$identity" ]] || return 1
  _validation_record_owned_path "$candidate" || return 1
  _validation_transition "${transition}-write" || return 1
  ln "$candidate" "$path" 2>/dev/null || return 1
  _validation_record_owned_path "$path" || return 1
  _validation_transition "${transition}-rename" || return 1
  _validation_transition "$transition" || return 1
  VALIDATION_CANDIDATE="$candidate"
  if ! $keep; then
    [[ "$(_validation_object_identity "$candidate" || true)" == "$identity" ]] || return 1
    rm -f "$candidate" || return 1
  fi

trigger: any piece of durable validation state is published during launch
outcome: every published state file is either fully and verifiably written, or the launch has an accurate record of exactly what it created to roll back
notes: Consequence-class: recovery — atomic publish plus ownership tracking makes an interrupted launch's exact progress reconstructable for rollback.

statement: Acquiring the validation launch lock uses an atomic hard-link (ln) creation, which can only succeed for one caller; on failure, exactly one stale-lock recovery attempt is made before giving up, so two competing launches for the same task/repo can never both believe they hold the lock.

source.quote:
for attempt in 1 2; do
    if ln "$candidate" "$VALIDATION_LAUNCH_LOCK" 2>/dev/null; then
      VALIDATION_LOCK_IDENTITY="$(_validation_path_identity "$VALIDATION_LAUNCH_LOCK")" || \
        return 1
      [[ "$VALIDATION_LOCK_IDENTITY" == "$identity" ]] || return 1
      VALIDATION_LOCK_OWNED=true
      rm -f "$candidate" || return 1
      return 0
    fi
    [[ "$attempt" -eq 1 ]] && _recover_validation_lock || return 1
  done
  return 1

trigger: two coordinators attempt to launch validation for the same task/repo concurrently
outcome: at most one validation launch is ever in-flight per task/repo at a time
notes: Consequence-class: delivery — a single-writer lease/lock ensures validation launch happens through exactly one path, never concurrently through two.

statement: The validation worker refuses to proceed unless the canonical validation intent's own current revision hash exactly matches the revision it was invoked with, before doing anything else.
trigger: sgt-validation-worker starts
outcome: a validation-worker invoked against a stale or mismatched intent revision fails immediately rather than running no-mistakes against the wrong intent
notes: Consequence-class: identity — intent identity re-verified again at this second re-entry point.

statement: The validation worker re-checks the coordinator's recorded intent transport decision against the actually-installed no-mistakes build's real capability, so a binary swapped between launch time and run time can neither downgrade the private intent-file transport into argv nor invoke a flag the installed build rejects; the recorded decision is honored exactly and never re-optimized here.

source.quote:
# Re-check the coordinator's recorded transport against the build that will
# actually run, so a binary swapped between launch and run can neither downgrade
# the private transport into argv nor invoke a flag this build rejects. The
# recorded decision is honoured exactly; it is never re-optimised here.
case "$INTENT_TRANSPORT" in
  intent-file|argv) ;;
  *)
    echo "ERROR: unsupported validation intent transport: $INTENT_TRANSPORT" >&2
    exit 2
    ;;
esac

trigger: sgt-validation-worker is about to run no-mistakes
outcome: the transport actually used can never silently diverge from what the coordinator recorded and the operator consented to, even across a binary swap
notes: Consequence-class: safety/human-decision — a recorded privacy/consent decision cannot be silently downgraded by an environment change.

statement: The validation worker treats the coordinator as alive only if the validation-launch lock file exists (and is not a symlink), its recorded pid responds to kill -0, and that pid's current process start time still matches what was recorded at lock-acquisition time.

source.quote:
_coordinator_is_alive() {
  local pid start current
  [[ -f "$REPO_STATE/validation-launch.lock" && \
    ! -L "$REPO_STATE/validation-launch.lock" ]] || return 1
  pid="$(_lock_field pid)" || return 1
  start="$(_lock_field start)" || return 1
  [[ "$pid" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] && kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null || return 1
  current="$(ps -o lstart= -p "$pid" 2>/dev/null | awk '{$1=$1; print}')"
  [[ -n "$current" && "$current" == "$start" ]]
}

trigger: the validation worker polls whether its coordinator is still alive
outcome: a reused PID is never mistaken for the still-live original coordinator
notes: Consequence-class: identity — PID-reuse-aware liveness check, mirroring the same pattern used for the lock owner elsewhere in this stage.

statement: The validation worker requires a live TMUX_PANE and a resolvable process start time for itself before publishing its own readiness handshake, and requires the coordinator to still be alive at that moment; the handshake value binds together the expected intent revision, the pane, the child PID, and the child's process start time.
trigger: the validation worker is ready to publish its readiness handshake
outcome: the readiness handshake cannot be published, or later replayed by an unrelated process, without matching this exact revision+pane+pid+start-time tuple
notes: Consequence-class: identity — a compound identity token binds every later handshake step to this specific process instance.

statement: Immediately before running no-mistakes, the validation worker verifies the isolated snapshot's current HEAD still matches the expected reviewed HEAD and that the snapshot is still validation-clean; either mismatch is a fatal error.

source.quote:
EXPECTED_HEAD="$(cat "$REPO_STATE/validation_head" 2>/dev/null || true)"

      "$(git -C "$WORKTREE" rev-parse HEAD 2>/dev/null || true)" != "$EXPECTED_HEAD" ]] || \
   ! _sgt_worktree_is_validation_clean "$WORKTREE"; then
    echo "ERROR: isolated validation code snapshot no longer matches reviewed HEAD" >&2
    exit 2
fi

trigger: the validation worker is about to run no-mistakes
outcome: no-mistakes never runs against a snapshot that changed after the coordinator captured it as the reviewed HEAD
notes: Consequence-class: identity — HEAD identity is re-verified a second time immediately before use, not trusted from an earlier check.

statement: Immediately before invoking no-mistakes, the validation worker re-computes the canonical intent's revision hash and fails (recording exited:2) if it no longer matches the expected revision, catching a content change made after the initial startup check rather than validating against it.

source.quote:
# Re-verify the canonical intent immediately before invoking no-mistakes, so a
# content change made after the startup check is caught rather than validated.
#
# Transport privacy: with the intent-file transport only the intent PATH reaches
# argv, so intent content never appears in ps or /proc/<pid>/cmdline. The argv
# transport does expose the content and is reachable only because the coordinator
# passed --allow-argv-intent for this run.
if [[ "$(_sgt_intent_revision "$VALIDATION_INTENT")" != "$EXPECTED_REVISION" ]]; then
  printf 'exited:2\n' > "$REPO_STATE/validation_status"
  echo "ERROR: canonical validation intent was modified after initial verification" >&2
  exit 2
fi

trigger: the validation worker is about to invoke no-mistakes
outcome: a TOCTOU intent modification between startup and invocation cannot slip through as if the originally-verified intent were still in force
notes: Consequence-class: identity — a second, immediately-pre-use re-verification closes the window a single startup-time check would leave open.

statement: With the intent-file transport only the intent's file PATH reaches no-mistakes' argv, so intent content never appears in ps or /proc/<pid>/cmdline; the argv transport is only reachable at all because the coordinator passed --allow-argv-intent, and it does expose the full intent content through those same surfaces.

source.quote:
if [[ "$INTENT_TRANSPORT" == "intent-file" ]]; then
  args=(axi run --intent-file "$VALIDATION_INTENT")
else
  # Consented argv transport: the operator accepted that intent content is
  # visible through ps and /proc/<pid>/cmdline for this run.
  args=(axi run --intent "$(cat "$VALIDATION_INTENT")")
fi

trigger: the validation worker assembles the no-mistakes invocation arguments
outcome: canonical intent content is process-list/proc-visible only when the operator specifically consented to that exposure for this run
notes: Consequence-class: human-decision/safety — the privacy-sensitive branch is only reachable through the recorded, consent-gated transport.

statement: The validation worker waits for the coordinator's validation-launch lock to be released before running no-mistakes, but if the coordinator process is found no longer alive while the lock file still exists, it fails rather than proceeding, unless the lock has genuinely already been removed by the time it checks.

source.quote:
while [[ -e "$REPO_STATE/validation-launch.lock" || \
  -L "$REPO_STATE/validation-launch.lock" ]]; do
  if ! _coordinator_is_alive; then
    [[ ! -e "$REPO_STATE/validation-launch.lock" && \
      ! -L "$REPO_STATE/validation-launch.lock" ]] && break
    exit 2
  fi
  sleep 0.05
done

_atomic_write() {

  local value="$2"

  printf '%s\n' "$value" > "$temporary"
  if ! mv "$temporary" "$target"; then
    rm -f "$temporary"
    return 1
  fi
}

_atomic_write_file() {
  local target="$1"
  local source_file="$2"
  local temporary
  temporary="$(mktemp "${target}.tmp.XXXXXX")"
  if ! cat "$source_file" > "$temporary" || ! mv "$temporary" "$target"; then
    rm -f "$temporary"
    return 1
